title: CAE’s reactions to SOTEU 2026
content:
Today’s State of the Union left us at Culture Action Europe with mixed feelings.  

On the one hand, from a cultural perspective, there was a lot we could recognise ourselves in: fighting together for our European idea, standing up for values, protecting Europe’s unique social model, and affirming that ‘in Europe, people will always come first.’  

 Culture runs through all of this. It is inseparable from Ukraine’s struggle to preserve its identity. From how we challenge narratives that divide us. From how children encounter the world and learn to use imagination. The proposed Congress of Europe feels like an obvious space for artists and cultural organisations to help shape a new vision for Europe.  

 On the other hand, concrete commitments to support the cultural sector were absent. Today marks 1099 days since cultural diversity was last mentioned in a 2023 SOTEU address. 

Today, a lot was said about AI and ‘the highest-quality data,’ which is ‘a precious European treasure,’ while ignoring that much of this data is sourced without asking or paying the authors and creators behind it.
